Twenty-six comments

The Maid I Ne’er Forgot

I was after this tune for ages. I originally heard it on the Arty McGlynn/Nollaig Casey album “Lead the Knave”, but it was only marked down as Eminor reel. I even got in touch with the publishers (Tara Music), but they didn’t know what it was and neither did Arty! I eventually stumbled across it by complete accident as an abc file on the web.

As with the album, I usually put t with Lads of Laois, but a major key tune such as Trip to Herve’s or Maid behind the Bar goes well with it.

↳ Posted by Bill on September 4th, 2001.

Still one of my favourite tunes after so many years.

↳ Posted by Gallowglass on October 24th, 2008.

A pure gem. Not often heard thesed days.
The melancholy and energy in it seem to match its name.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on April 28th, 2010.

Bm reel from Padraig Rynne

I’ve been wondering for a while about a name for the “Bm reel” on the last track of Padraig Rynne’s album “Bye a while”. Because the setting is different and it’s transposed so far up, it seems like a different tune. I always thought it was a modern composition, but then figured it would have been credited as such on the album sleeve notes. It always niggled because there was something familiar about the tune, so I eventually got round to transcribing it, and when I transposed it into the more likely key of E minor, I started playing it differently and realised I already knew the tune! Here is the Bm setting (note that his octave leaps have been simplified to held notes):

Re: The Maid I Never Forgot

John Gallagher makes great flat flutes. I have the first modern 8-keyed B flute (as far as I know), and John made it. It’s based on meticulous drawings of a couple Bb Rudall and Rose flutes, that he scaled up.

Matt’s flute is a Siccama-style band flute made by Hawkes, but because it’s high-pitch, it’s actually closer to B than Bb on quite a few tracks.

Re: “The Maid I Never Forgot” played on flute.

https://thesession.org/tunes/269
As far as I know, the original, historic key of this would have been E minor, and probably wasn’t played in B minor until Padraig Rynne recorded it in that key. There doesn’t appear to be any octave jumps in the E minor version posted, so any in the B minor version will probably have been inserted by Padraig Rynne as variations. I wouldn’t regard the octave jumps/drops as difficult, you just need to practice them.
I see that the tune has been recorded by Matt Molloy, Will Woodson and Paddy Carty. I will check those recordings but predict that all 3 flute players are playing in E minor rather than B minor. Seeing them on a Youtube video wouldn’t help much I would have thought . You need to listen.
Will Woodson : https://youtu.be/6N1W_9CLuJ4?si=zq9rgW3aspV99A1Z

The Maid I Never Forgot, X:8

Great transcription, Aberfoyle - I knew almost immediately it was the one I was looking for! Just wanted to point out that I think the high D in the first bar of the final line is actually a C# - it’s always stuck out to me as one of the defining features of Molloy’s version as, although it’s in keeping with the Dorian mode that the tune mostly seems to inhabit, the way it’s used as a momentary inflection in that phrase feels slightly unusual.
